items.title: #DataViz: Where does India shut down the internet?
items.summary: India saw more than 900 internet shutdowns in 15 years, which translates to a shutdown order every six days, on average, according to our analysis of data compiled by the Software Freedom Law Center (SFLC). Two in three of these were in Jammu and Kashmir, Rajasthan and Manipur. Preventive shutdowns, imposed in anticipation of an event, accounted for 70% (654) recorded incidents, while the rest were categorised as ‘reactive’. The longest shutdown in the tracker lasted 552 days in Jammu and Kashmir, where internet access was restricted from August 4, 2019, after the abrogation of Article 370, until 4G services were restored on February 6, 2021. Manipur’s statewide shutdown, imposed after violence broke out in May 2023, lasted 200 days. Recorded shutdowns fell from a peak of 136 in 2018 to 33 so far in 2026. Delhi recorded 11 internet shutdowns in 15 years, seven of them in 2026—as many as in Manipur and more than in any other state or Union territory this year. items.title: Another minor files complaint, ninth POCSO case registered against Veeramani
items.summary: The Greater Chennai Police (GCP) have registered a ninth case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act against Gem Granites chairman R Veeramani following a fresh complaint by another minor girl alleging sexual abuse. According to the police, the fresh case was registered on November 13 based on the statement of the survivor. The police have also arrested Perumal alias Bala, a former driver of Veeramani, for allegedly bringing minor girls to him and facilitating the offences. He was arrested on Saturday, November 14, and remanded to judicial custody at the Puzhal Central Prison. With the latest case, nine POCSO cases have been registered against Veeramani, involving 13 minor girls. Ten people, including Veeramani, have been arrested in connection with the cases. Separately, Veeramani was booked in 2004 for allegedly abetting the suicide of a minor girl. A chargesheet was filed on November 11 in one of the nine POCSO cases, with the trial set to commence. The case also names former Chennai Police Commissioner Arun as an accused. Meanwhile, the SIT on Saturday conducted a search at Veeramani's residence in Royapettah, Chennai, following a survivor's statement
